newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arafat says nothing suggests agreement with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says nothing suggests agreement with Israel.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat said on Friday he saw nothing to suggest agreement was possible with the Israeli government on the West Bank town of Hebron.

"There's no sign of hope that in the future a solution will be reached that satisfies the Palestinian side, especially in view of the Israeli government's intransigence," he told reporters on arrival at Cairo airport.

Israel and the Palestinians have been negotiating on and off for months on an Israeli redeployment in Hebron. The Israelis often say agreement is close but the Palestinians say the talks make no progress.

Arafat, on his way home from a visit to Europe, met Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Cairo and then left for home in Gaza, official sources said. No details of his talks with the Egyptian leader were available.
On arrival, he said: "I will listen to his (Mubarak's) advice, especially as the negotiations are paralysed now, because Israel has not implemented any of the articles (of previous agreements)."
He complained again that Israel was confiscating Palestinian land, building settlements and arresting Palestinians.

The United States, concerned at the lack of progress in the Middle East peace process, is sending special envoy Dennis Ross back to the region at the weekend, Secretary of State Warren Christopher said on Thursday.
Christopher told a year-end news conference the risk of fresh acts of violence in the Middle East made it essential to "regain and restore momentum" in the peace process.
